Check a table is in taxonAlign's taxonomic reference format

Source: R/taxonomic_reference_schema.R
check_taxonomic_reference.Rd

Checks a reference table against taxonomic_reference_schema(): every required column is present, every record has a name, rank, status, dataset and ID, taxon_ID is unique, and every record leads somewhere in the table – an accepted record to itself, any other to another record's taxon_ID. Every data release load_taxonomic_resources() downloads passes this check.

Usage

check_taxonomic_reference(x, name = deparse(substitute(x)))

Arguments

x

A data frame.

name

What to call x in the error message. Defaults to the expression passed as x.

Value

x, invisibly, if it passes. Otherwise an error listing every problem found.

Details

prepare_taxonomic_resources() is more forgiving than this: it renames Darwin Core columns, and drops (with a warning) a record with no canonical_name. Use this check on a reference you're going to share or release, so that other people get the same results from it that you do.

Examples

reference <- data.frame(
  canonical_name = c("Boronia serrulata", "Boronia oldname"),
  scientific_name = c("Boronia serrulata Sm.", "Boronia oldname Sm."),
  taxon_rank = "species", taxonomic_status = c("accepted", "synonym"),
  taxonomic_dataset = "MY_LIST", genus = "Boronia",
  taxon_ID = c("1", "2"), accepted_name_usage_ID = c("1", "1")
)
check_taxonomic_reference(reference)
